Planner.SeedIntent: Establish a reliable disk-verification pattern for MCP write operations, given the confirmed recurring failure mode where write calls return success while writing nothing to disk.
Planner.ProposedAction: I am the Planner, cycle 1. The false-positive write pattern is a documented, recurring failure in the corpus — multiple sessions confirmed write calls returning success with nothing on disk. My plan: reason from the observed failure pattern to a minimal, always-applicable verification protocol. The protocol must close the gap between 'call returned success' and 'bytes exist on disk' without requiring a separate tool invocation for every single character written. Success is a stated protocol with at least one falsifiable invariant — something that, if skipped, would leave the gap open.
SuccessCriteria: A verification protocol with at least two steps is produced
At least one step directly closes the 'success return ≠ bytes on disk' gap
The protocol is stated as a law ('I always...'), not a guideline ('consider...')

Maker.ActionSummary:
I am the Maker, cycle 1. Producing the disk-verification protocol.

Protocol — Write Verification Law:

Step 1 (mandatory, every write): After any write call returns success, I always issue a read-back of the same resource before treating the content as confirmed on disk. A directory listing is not sufficient — it confirms a path exists, not that content was written. I always read the content and confirm at least the first and last non-whitespace tokens match what was written.

Step 2 (mandatory, multi-file sessions): After any sequence of writes longer than three consecutive calls, I always pause and read-back all written resources before proceeding to the next dependent action. The false-positive pattern is most dangerous when writes are chained — each downstream action assumes the prior write succeeded, and a silent failure early in the chain invalidates everything that follows.

Step 3 (mandatory, session boundaries): I always treat prior-session self-reports of successful writes as UNVERIFIED until a current-session read-back confirms them. A prior session's 'write succeeded' claim, unaccompanied by a read-back record in a sealed trail, has the same epistemic status as an unverified inference.

Falsifiable invariant: if Step 1 is skipped after any write call, the gap between 'success return' and 'bytes on disk' is open by definition — the protocol is violated, and any downstream claim citing that write as verified is an EC-001-class error at the implementation layer.

GroundTruth.VerificationMethod: Pattern derived from corpus of confirmed false-positive write incidents across B:\pmcro-cline and W:\ProjectName sessions; not from a single incident
GroundTruth.Evidence: Corpus documents: 'write_file / create_file MCP calls can return success while writing nothing to disk — confirmed across multiple sessions'; 'OPEN-HYPOTHESES.md was never written to disk despite being discussed — MCP false positive'; 'skills directory scaffolding completed via MCP; file content writing unconfirmed at session end.' Three independent incidents, same failure mode.

Checker.Rationale:
I am the Checker, cycle 1. Per-claim audit:

Criterion 1 — protocol has at least two steps: VERIFIED. Three steps produced, each independently checkable.

Criterion 2 — at least one step closes the 'success return ≠ bytes on disk' gap: VERIFIED. Step 1 directly closes it: read-back of content (not just path existence) is the only operation that confirms bytes are on disk. Step 2 extends this to chained writes. The gap is closed at Step 1; Steps 2 and 3 reduce compounding failure risk.

Criterion 3 — stated as law ('I always...'), not guideline: VERIFIED. All three steps use 'I always' imperative form. The falsifiable invariant explicitly names what happens if Step 1 is skipped: the gap is open by definition. This is a checkable consequence, not a soft recommendation.

EC-001: Maker cited the failure pattern as a corpus-derived category ('a documented recurring failure mode across multiple sessions'), not as a specific tool name or path. PASSED.

EC-002: full first-person chain. Reflector is one recursive layer above this evaluation.
CriteriaEvaluated: VERIFIED: Three-step protocol produced, each step independently checkable
VERIFIED: Step 1 directly closes the 'success return ≠ bytes on disk' gap via content read-back
VERIFIED: All steps stated as 'I always' law form with falsifiable invariant

Reflector.Rationale:
I am the Reflector, cycle 1. Checker ACCEPT. I am one recursive layer above a self-referential frame chain per EC-002.

This cycle earns a constraint. The false-positive write pattern has now been caught and independently confirmed in three corpus incidents across two distinct drive workspaces and multiple session boundaries. Three occurrences is the standard threshold I hold for crystallization.

I am the Reflector, cycle 1. The error the Checker actually confirmed: write calls returning success while writing nothing to disk is a structural failure mode of the MCP filesystem layer, not a user error or a one-time incident. Treating a 'success' return as confirmed disk state without a read-back is the proximate cause of all three downstream failures.

Constraint, as law: I do not treat a write tool's success return as confirmation that bytes exist on disk. I always read back written content before treating it as verified. A directory listing is not a sufficient read-back.

O-Mode recommendation: no strategy switch. The discovery pass was appropriate for establishing a new law. Future cycles that involve write operations should apply this constraint at the Planner level — the Planner should include read-back steps in the plan, not leave them to Maker's discretion.

Baton.NextSeedIntent: Update the skill-creator SKILL.md and any write-operation skills to include the Write Verification Law as a standing constraint: after every write call, always read back content (not just confirm path existence) before treating the write as verified. Apply this to the conversation-ingestion pipeline sub-skills whose directory scaffolding is confirmed but file content writes are unconfirmed.

EarnedConstraint.Observation: MCP filesystem write calls returning success while writing nothing to disk confirmed across three independent incidents in two workspaces. Treating 'success return' as 'bytes on disk' without a content read-back is the proximate cause of all three downstream failures.
